title: SSH keys and least-privilege sudo
subtitle: Replace password guessing with keys, then delegate exactly the commands an operator needs — no more.
objectives: Create an SSH key pair and protect the private key
Install a public key for key-based authentication
Explain the permissions SSH requires on .ssh and authorized_keys
Write a scoped sudoers drop-in and validate it safely
Choose between wheel membership and command-specific sudo rules

ex200.evidence: ssh-keygen with an explicit key path and no passphrase in a lab.
authorized_keys contains the public key, not the private key.
Correct modes on ~/.ssh and authorized_keys; sshd -t.
visudo -cf validates a drop-in with a command allowlist.
Compare %wheel ALL=(ALL) ALL with a scoped command rule.

versionNotes: RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 both use OpenSSH and system-wide crypto policies. RHEL 10 has newer OpenSSH defaults, so generate modern key types rather than relying on old RSA settings.
RHEL 10 continues to support sudoers drop-ins in /etc/sudoers.d; use visudo -cf and mode 0440 on both releases.

commands.desc: Create a modern SSH key pair with a descriptive comment.
Install the public key on a remote account.
Apply the modes SSH expects for key material.
Validate the sshd configuration before restarting it.
Syntax-check a sudoers drop-in without opening an editor.
Validate the main sudoers file and drop-ins.
Allow the webops group to restart only httpd.
Show the effective sudo rules for a user.

lab.title: Keys for access, sudo for one job
lab.scenario: Create a dedicated key, place its public half correctly, create the webops group, and grant it one scoped sudo command. Validate every layer.

steps.text: Generate an ed25519 key pair for the student account without a passphrase in this disposable lab.
steps.verify: The private key exists with mode 0600 and the public key with mode 0644.

steps.text: Install the public key into authorized_keys and correct the directory/file modes.
steps.verify: authorized_keys starts with ssh-ed25519 and is readable only by the owner.

steps.text: Create the webops group and add student to it.
steps.cmd: sudo groupadd webops && sudo usermod -aG webops student
steps.verify: id student lists webops in the supplementary groups.

steps.text: Create a scoped sudoers drop-in that lets webops restart httpd only.
steps.cmd: printf "%s\n" "%webops ALL=(ALL) /usr/bin/systemctl restart httpd" | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/webops && sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/webops
steps.verify: The file is mode 0440 and contains only the intended command rule.

steps.text: Validate sudoers and inspect the effective rule for student.
steps.verify: visudo reports parsed OK and sudo -l shows the scoped systemctl command without full sudo.

quiz.q: Which file must contain the public key for key-based SSH login?
quiz.why: The remote account’s authorized_keys holds the public key that matches the client’s private key.

quiz.q: Why should the private key be mode 0600?
options: SSH refuses overly permissive key material because it could be stolen
quiz.why: OpenSSH rejects keys readable by other users; the private key must remain private.

quiz.q: What is the safest way to delegate one systemctl command through sudo?
options: Give the user the root password
Use a sudoers rule with the full command path and no wildcard
quiz.why: A command-specific rule follows least privilege and avoids granting unrelated root access.
